title: Military Deployment Against BLM Protesters - Insurrection Act Threat and Martial Law Preparation
description_short: Military Deployment Against BLM Protesters - Insurrection Act Threat and Martial Law Preparation
description_medium: During racial-justice protests in June 2020, Trump threatened to deploy “heavily armed” military personnel if state governors did not “dominate” demonstrations. He also called for aggressive force against protesters, and federal officers cleared Lafayette Square before his walk to St. John’s Church. The record combines that threat and the clearing with broader claims of martial-law preparation; it does not establish that martial law was declared or that the Insurrection Act was invoked.
description_long: Donald Trump threatened to deploy active military forces against Black Lives Matter protesters under Insurrection Act while clearing peaceful demonstrators with tear gas for photo opportunity at St. John's Church, demonstrating systematic preparation for martial law implementation and military suppression of constitutional assembly rights during racial justice demonstrations. The comprehensive military deployment threat included Trump's June 1, 2020 Rose Garden speech declaring himself 'law and order president' while promising to deploy 'heavily armed soldiers, military personnel, and law enforcement officers' against protesters if governors failed to 'dominate' demonstrations through violent suppression. The martial law preparation extended to systematic military buildup around Washington D.C. while Trump demanded governors use 'overwhelming force' against protesters, creating atmosphere of military occupation designed to suppress constitutional assembly rights through systematic intimidation and threatened violence against racial justice demonstrations. Trump's military deployment threats violated Posse Comitatus Act and constitutional assembly protections by systematically threatening to use armed forces against civilian protesters while preparing martial law implementation that would suspend constitutional rights during peaceful demonstrations for racial justice and police reform. The Insurrection Act threats created precedent for military suppression of constitutional rights while demonstrating systematic willingness to use armed forces against American citizens exercising First Amendment assembly rights during legitimate protests against racial injustice and police violence. The military protest suppression established Trump's systematic approach to constitutional rights and racial justice movements, demonstrating willingness to use martial law threats while deploying military force against peaceful protesters who challenged systemic racism and police violence through constitutional assembly and democratic participation.

title: Trump: Lara Trump announces she's now a paid contributor for Fox News
description_short: Trump: Lara Trump announces she's now a paid contributor for Fox News
description_medium: On March 29, 2021, Lara Trump announced that Fox News had hired her as a paid contributor. She said she was excited to join and joked she had felt like an unofficial member of the network after appearing there frequently. Fox’s hiring followed Kayleigh McEnany’s move from White House press secretary to the network; other former Trump-world figures were appearing at rival Newsmax. The announcement documented a media role, not any particular editorial assignment or impact on coverage.
description_long: Lara Trump announced on March 29, 2021, that she had signed a paid contributor contract with Fox News. She described herself as excited to join the network and said she had long felt like an unofficial member because she appeared there so often. The announcement formalized her relationship with a broadcaster where she had already been a regular guest. As Donald Trump’s daughter-in-law and a prominent campaign surrogate, her new role placed a close family member of the former president inside a major television news organization. Fox also hired former White House press secretary Kayleigh McEnany after she left the Trump administration. Other Trump allies, including Jason Miller, Andrew Giuliani, Sean Spicer and Steve Bannon, appeared on or worked with rival Newsmax. The move illustrates the migration of political figures into television roles after the 2020 election. The available facts establish Lara Trump’s paid contributor position, but do not specify its contract terms, assignments, or influence on Fox’s reporting.

title: Trump: On Veep call with Trump, JD Vance tells son to ‘shut the hell up'
description_short: Trump: On Veep call with Trump, JD Vance tells son to ‘shut the hell up'
description_medium: Vance later said that when Trump called to tell him he had been selected as the 2024 running mate, he asked his son to stop talking while he took the call. Vance described the child talking about Pokémon cards in their hotel room and said the call was the most important of his life. The anecdote comes from Vance’s podcast retelling.
description_long: Donald Trump called J.D. Vance on July 15, 2024, to tell him he had selected him as his running mate, on the opening day of the Republican National Convention. Vance later described the moment on the Full Send Podcast. He said he and his family were in a hotel room, where his son wanted to talk about Pokémon cards; Vance told him to be quiet for 30 seconds so he could take what he called the most important phone call of his life. The account is Vance’s own later retelling, rather than an independently recorded version of the family’s exchange. The source pairs the story with Vance’s earlier criticism of “childless cat ladies” and his claims about family values. That juxtaposition supplies the political context for the anecdote, though the brief exchange itself is personal rather than an official action. The incident records how Vance narrated his reaction to becoming Trump’s vice-presidential pick.

title: Trump tells Trudeau ‘Canada could be America's 51st state'
description_short: Trump tells Trudeau ‘Canada could be America's 51st state'
description_medium: Donald Trump reportedly suggested that Canada become a U.S. state during a November 29, 2024 meeting with Prime Minister Justin Trudeau at Mar-a-Lago. Fox News attributed the remark to anonymous sources and placed it in a discussion of threatened tariffs, border security and trade. The same report said Trump joked Trudeau could instead become a state governor. There is no transcript or evidence of a formal proposal.
description_long: Fox News reported that Donald Trump raised the idea of Canada becoming the 51st U.S. state during a November 29, 2024 meeting with Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau at Mar-a-Lago. The report attributed the exchange to anonymous people familiar with the meeting, not to a transcript or on-the-record participant. According to those sources, the discussion followed Trump’s threat to impose tariffs on Canadian goods and covered border security and trade. Trump reportedly joked that Trudeau could become a state governor, prompting nervous laughter from those present. The reported remarks were not accompanied by a formal proposal, an agreement between the governments, or a change in Canada’s status. The account is a description of an exchange during a meeting between the leaders, and its wording and context remain dependent on anonymous reporting. It documents no policy action toward annexation; the statehood comment is best treated as a reported remark rather than an official position or plan.
notes: Reason: The account relies on anonymous sources and provides no transcript or on-the-record confirmation of the exact wording.

title: Trump pardons Dark Web drug trafficker, money launderer
description_short: Trump pardons Dark Web drug trafficker, money launderer
description_medium: On January 21, 2025, Trump granted Ross Ulbricht an unconditional pardon. Ulbricht created the Silk Road, an online marketplace used to sell drugs and other illegal services, and had been serving a life sentence after a jury convicted him on drug trafficking, money laundering conspiracy and other charges. Trump said the conviction was politically motivated; the pardon ended the federal sentence.
description_long: Trump issued an unconditional pardon to Ross Ulbricht on January 21, 2025, his second day in office. Ulbricht created Silk Road, a dark-web marketplace that operated from 2011 until it was seized by the FBI in 2013. A jury convicted him of drug distribution, conspiracy to commit money laundering and other offenses; in 2015 he received a life sentence. Trump announced the pardon on Truth Social and called Ulbricht’s prosecution politically motivated, describing the officials involved as part of what he called the weaponization of government against him. Ulbricht later described the pardon as a victory for people who value freedom. The clemency action ended Ulbricht’s federal prison sentence. It did not erase the jury’s verdict or establish that the conviction had been wrongful. The event is a presidential pardon, with Trump’s political explanation and Ulbricht’s reaction distinct from the factual record of the prosecution and sentence.
